ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure is a pendulum-type friction coefficient measuring instrument, which can measure the dynamic friction coefficient between the tire and the ground. Its main components include: a pendulum with a tire rubber sheet fixed at the bottom and a lightweight thin rod connected to the pendulum. The mass of the pendulum is $m$, and the thin rod can rotate freely in the vertical plane around the axis $O$. The distance from the center of gravity of the pendulum to point $O$ is $L$. During measurement, the instrument is fixed on a horizontal ground, and the pendulum is released from rest at a position level with $O$. When the pendulum reaches near the lowest point, the rubber sheet tightly presses the ground and slides over a small distance $s$ ($s \ll L$), after which it continues to swing to the highest position at an angle $\theta$ with the vertical direction. If the pressure of the pendulum on the ground can be considered as a constant force of magnitude $F$, and the gravitational acceleration is $g$.

1. The mechanical energy lost by the pendulum in the aforementioned process
2. The work done by friction on the pendulum during the above process
3. The kinetic friction coefficient between the rubber sheet and the ground.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a bracket and a dial, and the rotating shaft is labeled O; the light rod can rotate about O in the vertical plane. Near the pendulum bob on the right side is marked mass m, and at the bottom of the pendulum bob is marked rubber sheet (Rubber sheet). From O to the direction of the center of gravity of the pendulum bob is marked distance L. The figure also draws the swinging trajectory and the angle θ with the vertical direction; near the ground at the bottom is marked the small distance s over which the rubber sheet slides on the ground, and the device is fixed on a horizontal base. Reasoning: According to the problem statement and method, take the gravitational potential energy when the center of gravity of the pendulum bob moves to the lowest point as zero. When the pendulum bob is released from rest, its center of gravity is at the same height as O, therefore the height relative to the lowest point is L, and the initial mechanical energy is E_initial = mgL. When the pendulum bob finally reaches the highest position, it is also instantaneously at rest, forming an angle θ with the vertical direction; at this time the height of the center of gravity relative to the lowest point is L(1 - cosθ), so the final mechanical energy is E_final = mgL(1 - cosθ). The loss of mechanical energy is ΔE_loss = E_initial - E_final = mgL - mgL(1 - cosθ) = mgL cosθ. The non-conservative dissipative work in the process is mainly the work done by friction, so the work done by the friction force on the pendulum bob is equal to the change in mechanical energy: W_f = E_final - E_initial = -mgL cosθ. The magnitude of the sliding friction force between the rubber sheet and the ground is μF, the sliding distance is s, and the friction work is W_f = -μFs. Comparing with the above formula gives μFs = mgL cosθ, therefore μ = mgL cosθ/(Fs).
